conditions.question: How settled is the bet this work rests on?

enablement.action: check whether a business can deliver an offering its customers value and earn more than providing it costs
enablement.actor: whoever starts, runs or funds the business
enablement.timing: before committing money or time to the business, and again whenever its customers, delivery or income change

guidance.claim: Fill in all nine blocks: customer segments, value propositions, channels, customer relationships, revenue streams, key resources, key activities, key partnerships and cost structure.
When a block does not apply, keep it and write in it why it does not apply.
For a new business every block is still a guess, and this canvas checks that the guesses fit together. The Lean Canvas picks which guess to test first; the Startup Canvas commits the venture's aims.
Segment by shared job or behaviour, not demographics alone — demographic-only segments are the classic false-precision trap.
In B2B the buyer, the user and the payer differ; healthtech's patient/provider/payer triangle makes single-segment framing misleading.
One beachhead segment. A long segment list this early signals unvalidated focus.

Distinct from Canonical Model: a segment here is a group of people the offering is for; a category there is one the system uses to sort its own data, such as account types. Ask whether it is about whom we serve or how the system files things.

sections.name: Customer segments
sections.question: Exactly which groups is the offering for?

guidance.claim: Always relative to the segment's current alternative, including doing nothing.
One per segment. A single all-segment value proposition usually means the segments were never really split.
Quantify in time, cost or risk. Where there is no market, qualitative is fine — but still name the alternative.

sections.name: Value proposition
sections.question: Why would a segment choose the offering over its alternatives?

guidance.claim: Cover every stage at which the offering meets the segment: how they hear of it, weigh it up, buy it, receive it and get support afterwards.
Product-led versus sales-led growth is at bottom a channels choice. Regulated and enterprise markets often have imposed channels — brokers, distributors, procurement — that dominate the design.
For physical goods, delivery and service channels drive cost structure. Link the two.

sections.name: Channels
sections.question: How does the offering reach each segment?

guidance.claim: For each segment, name the kind of relationship: personal assistance, dedicated personal assistance, self-service, automated service, community or co-creation.
Skipping this hides how you keep people once they arrive. For each segment, say what keeps them coming back or staying.

sections.name: Customer relationships
sections.question: What kind of relationship do we keep with each segment?

guidance.claim: Core to the Business Model Canvas and the Lean Canvas. Strategy canvases often omit it, treating monetisation as downstream of positioning.
In regulated industries this is often fixed by regulation or reimbursement codes. Record it as a constraint, not a choice.
A hypothesis to test, not a plan. Deep tech and hardware commonly defer it until technical maturity.

sections.name: Revenue streams
sections.question: How does the offering earn money?

guidance.claim: Check all four kinds of key resource: physical, intellectual (brand, patents, data), human and financial.
Deep tech, EV and robotics are dominated by intellectual property and specialised equipment. Licences and certifications carry lead times — flag them early.
Software businesses often run thin here. Thin is an answer, not a gap.

sections.name: Key resources
sections.question: What assets must we own or control?

guidance.claim: List only what you must do yourselves; any activity someone else does for you belongs in Key Partnerships.
Distinct from Capabilities: activities are what you do, capabilities are what you must be able to do. Strategy canvases use the latter.

sections.name: Key activities
sections.question: Which activities must we perform ourselves?

guidance.claim: For each partner, say what you rely on them for, such as supply, integration, resale or a platform you run on.
For platform-dependent products the platform is a partnership with unilateral terms. Track it as a risk too.
In construction and hardware, partner schedules land directly on the critical path.

sections.name: Key partnerships
sections.question: What do we deliberately rely on others for?

guidance.claim: The dominant driver is the insight, not the line items — services and construction run on per-project labour, software on headcount, hardware on cost of goods sold and capex.
Distinguish fixed from variable and note what scales with growth. The growth mechanism can invert the shape.
Still applies at personal and household scale, where time is the usual dominant cost.

sections.name: Cost structure
sections.question: What mainly determines the cost of providing the offering?
